complexity.notes: The signature is computed twice per word; a single pass with dict.setdefault(sig, []).append(word) would halve the work. ord(letter)-97 is clearer as ord(letter)-ord('a'). The annotation '-> tuple(int)' would raise under eager evaluation on older Pythons, but PEP 649 on CPython 3.14 defers it, so it is harmless here. Worst case reflects adversarial collisions on the input-controlled count-tuple keys; with the stated 3-8 char word lengths the signature space is bounded and this does not materialize.
complexity.summary: Each word is mapped to a 26-element character-count tuple used as its anagram signature, and words are grouped in a dict keyed by that signature. The solution makes two passes (one to seed the dict, one to append), computing the signature twice per word.
